evidence: src/infrastructure/in-memory-task-repository.ts: the InMemoryTaskRepository class implements TaskRepository using a private Map<string, Task> as its storage, which is persistence work and fits the infrastructure layer
save(task) calls this.items.set(task.id, task), and findById(id) calls this.items.get(id). Both are plain storage reads and writes.
findByProject(projectId, filter) only matches stored items against the projectId, status and assigneeId criteria. This is query execution, not a domain rule.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file sits in the infrastructure layer and has one job: persisting Task entities. It does this as an in-memory adapter for the domain port TaskRepository. save and findById only store and read entries in a Map. findByProject turns the query criteria from TaskFilter (projectId, plus optional status and assigneeId) into a filter over the stored items. That is query logic a database adapter would express as a WHERE clause, not a business rule. The file contains no invariants, state transitions, authorization or other domain decisions, so everything in it belongs to infrastructure.
